newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - OCT 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - OCT 25.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The government opts to impose new tax on real estate holdings worth more than 100 million drachmas with the aim of raising revenues for state coffers and confirming the socialist identity of the ruling party.
--At the same time, the government is still considering a 15 percent tax on revenues arising from transactions on financial products.
--Halyvourgiki moves to further reduce production and staff in face of an uncertain future. Two hundred workers face voluntary retirement or the sack.
--Transport and Communications Minister Haris Kastanidis announces increasing investment interest in telecommunications networks and services at Thessaloniki conference.
--General Bank - the fourth state-run bank in a row - returns reduced profits for first half 1996.
IMERISIA

--The government is looking at imposing a tax which will result in raising the cost of loans in foreign exchange for business and consumers, in an effort to ensure a further drop in the inflation rate.
--Greece forwards requests for Cohesion Fund financing of 15 road projects with a total estimated cost of 108 billion drachmas.

--Invitations to bid for the sale of the Bank of Crete will be published within the next 10 days. The Bank of Greece and the national economy minister estimate that the bank will go for some 40 billion drachmas.
KERDOS

--The national economy ministry looks at rationalising the use of the state's property. A meeting chaired by minister Yannos Papandoniou is told that the state spends over 20 billion drachmas in rents to house government services while it owns 42 million stremmata of real estate worth seven trillion drachmas.

--Government hopes to bring in 45 billion drachmas in the first stage of implementing the 15 percent tax on financial products. Also being considered is a tax on interest on forex deposits as well as the deregulation of the foreign exchange market with the abolition of restrictions on forex deposits with domestic banks.
--The new budget is aiming at 8.5 trillion drachmas in revenues, sources say. Reports add that the 1996 budget will fall short by 150 billion drachmas.
EXPRESS

--Goals for the 1997 budget defined at hours-long meeting chaired by Papandoniou yesterday: increase in revenues from 13 to 14 percent, spending cutbacks of 150 billion drachmas and containment of deficit in the new budget to 4.2 percent.

--The development ministry and experts are drafting a new improved law on competition, which is expected to constitute the basic institutional tool in the modernisation of commerce. --Elefsina shipyards face imminent privatisation or closure as European Commission notes that only one shipyard (Skaramangas) can be half-owned by the state.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Ergo Bank considering a proposal for cooperation with foreign bank - with no more than a 20 percent stake in share capital - to expand activities.
--National Bank looks at new measures to settle debts in the framework of expanding its portfolio.
--Public debt: this year's interest bill will be close to the 3.6 trillion drachma mark, 400 billion more than convergence programme targets and 250 billion more than the budget targets.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
